# How To Suck — fully generated by AI

## Description

How To Suck is an experimental first-person cooperative Unity game for **1–4 players** about a crew of cleaners equipped with absurdly powerful vacuum cleaners. Players explore locations, suck up valuables, fire collected objects at enemies, and haul their loot back to a truck. Every contract requires meeting a delivery quota and defeating a boss — whose body also has to be delivered.

**The entire project was generated by GPT-6 Astra, without human involvement in development.** Code, 3D models, animations, environments, gameplay systems, UI, and multiplayer were created by the AI. This project continues the experiment of finding out whether AI can independently create a complete video game.

Sound effects were generated using **ElevenLabs** and checked with locally running **Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct** and **LAION CLAP** models.

| Experiment | Details |
| --- | --- |
| AI model | **GPT-6 Astra**, working through Codex |
| Human development work | **None — fully generated by AI** |
| Subscription usage | **2 full weekly usage limits on a Pro x20 subscription** |
| First autonomous iteration | **39 hours — 1 day and 15 hours** |

The 39-hour figure refers to the **first iteration**. The two weekly limits cover the project's development, including subsequent iterations.

Watch the creation process on YouTube: [Watch the Creation Process](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tvfLzNi_Xsw)

## Download and Play the Build

1. Go to the [How To Suck page on itch.io](https://breineng.itch.io/how-to-suck).
2. Download the Windows build archive.
3. Extract the entire archive to a folder on your computer.
4. Run `How to Suck.exe` to start the game.
5. Play solo, or host an online room and share its code with your friends.

## Installation from Source

1. Install **Git LFS** and clone this repository using its GitHub **Code** button URL.
2. In the project root, download and verify the binary assets:

   ```shell
   git lfs install
   git lfs pull
   git lfs fsck
   ```

3. Open the project in **Unity Editor 6000.3.6f1** and wait for assets and packages to finish importing.
4. Open `Assets/_Game/Production/Scenes/ProductBootstrap.unity` and press **Play**, or use **How to Suck → Играть** in the Unity menu.
5. Choose solo play to run the game locally. **Solo does not require EOS credentials or Steam.**
6. To build the game, select **Windows x64** in Unity and keep the enabled scenes in their existing build order.

### Online Multiplayer Setup

The project uses **Epic Online Services (EOS)** for online rooms by default and also includes a Steam networking provider.

- For EOS, configure your own game client and place its configuration in `.local/eos-client.json`. This local configuration is excluded from Git.
- Select the provider through **How to Suck → Networking → Select Epic Online Services** or **Select Steam**, outside Play Mode.
- All players must use compatible builds with the same provider and service configuration.

The configuration schema, build behavior, and Steam setup are documented in the [Networking Guide](docs/networking/EPIC_SETUP_RU.md). Without an EOS configuration, a source build supports solo play but cannot create EOS online rooms.

See [Running and Building](docs/UNITY_TOOLING.md) for additional setup details.

## Gameplay

- **Solo or up to 4 players:** create a room and invite friends using a room code.
- **Vacuum-based physics:** pull objects toward the nozzle, collect what fits, and move oversized cargo through the environment.
- **Loot doubles as ammunition:** store collected objects and fire them at enemies. The same valuables you need to deliver can help you survive.
- **Contracts and extraction:** deliver enough value to the truck, defeat the boss, and transport its body before the contract timer runs out.
- **Three locations:** Old House, Supermarket, and Warehouse, with **six contracts** across two chapters.
- **Equipment progression:** unlock vacuum cleaners from **MK1 to MK4** and upgrade storage capacity separately.
- **Persistent progress:** campaign saves, local settings, and personal achievements.
- **17 language options:** English, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Spanish (Spain), Spanish (Latin America), Portuguese (Brazil), German, French, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Czech, Turkish, Thai, Ukrainian, and Italian.

## Technology and Architecture

The game uses **Unity 6000.3.6f1**, **C#**, and the **Universal Render Pipeline (URP)**. Multiplayer simulation runs on **Netcode for GameObjects**, with EOS and Steam transports for online play. The AI created the game's 3D models and animations in **Blender**.

### Architecture

| System | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Authoritative simulation | `AuthorityWorld` owns world simulation; the host validates inventory changes, damage, deliveries, and contract results |
| Player input | `PlayerInputReader` captures local input and submits player intentions to the simulation |
| Suction and storage | `SuctionSystem`, `IngestionService`, and `PlayerStorage` handle suction, collection, and stored cargo |
| Object combat | `ItemFireService` validates shots, launches stored objects, and processes impacts |
| Contracts and progression | `ContractController` and `ProgressionService` manage objectives, results, and campaign progression |
| Data-driven content | ScriptableObject definitions for contracts, vacuum cleaners, loot, and enemies |
| Networking | `NetworkConnectionCoordinator` manages local and online connections; runtime gameplay is separated from online service SDKs |
| Persistence | Separate repositories for campaign saves, local settings, and achievement profiles |

### Scenes

Production scenes are located in `Assets/_Game/Production/Scenes`.

| Scene | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `ProductBootstrap` | Game startup and entry point |
| `ProductEntry` | Main menu and session entry |
| `ProductLobby` | Campaign lobby, contract selection, and equipment |
| `OldHouseNetwork` | Old House contracts |
| `SupermarketNetwork` | Supermarket contracts |
| `WarehouseNetwork` | Warehouse contracts |

### Networking

- **Netcode for GameObjects 2.13.2** synchronizes gameplay state.
- **Epic Online Services** provides online lobbies and P2P connections with room codes.
- **Steamworks.NET** provides the alternative Steam lobby and networking integration.
- **Unity Transport 2.6.0** supports the local solo host.
- Clients submit input; the host confirms changes and replicates the resulting state.
- Players join in the lobby. Leaving as the host ends the session; host migration is not implemented.

### UI and Localization

The interface uses **Unity UI (uGUI)** and **TextMesh Pro**, with settings, input rebinding, contract selection, equipment screens, and an in-game HUD. Language selection supports manual preferences, Steam language detection, and system-language fallback.

### Audio Production and Evaluation

- **[ElevenLabs Sound Effects](https://elevenlabs.io/sound-effects):** sound-effect generation, followed by local editing and additional synthesis.
- **[Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct):** local audio analysis and descriptions of the sounds present in generated clips.
- **[LAION CLAP](https://huggingface.co/laion/clap-htsat-fused)** (`laion/clap-htsat-fused`): local comparison of audio clips against text descriptions to assess how closely they matched the intended sound.
- Model evaluations were supplemented with signal measurements, including duration, peak levels, and clipping checks.

## Requirements

- **Windows 64-bit** for the downloadable build.
- **Unity 6000.3.6f1** for development, with Windows build support for a Windows build.
- **Git LFS** to download the project's binary assets.
- Internet access for restoring Unity packages and playing online.
- An EOS game-client configuration or a configured Steam application for online multiplayer in your own builds.
